packet.headline_seed: Oil prices slide on hopes of US-Iran peace deal
packet.description_seed: Trump said on Saturday that an agreement would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, without giving further details.

what: Oil prices slide on hopes of US-Iran peace deal

clean_source_blocks.text: Oil prices have fallen sharply and Asian stock markets have risen on hopes of a deal that could bring an end to the US-Israel war with Iran. On Saturday, US President Donald Trump said an agreement with Tehran had been "largely negotiated" and details would be announced soon but the following day urged his negotiating team not to rush a deal. On Monday in Asia, global oil benchmark Brent was down by 5.5% at $97.90 (£72.64), while US-traded crude was 5.9% lower at $90.93. Trump had previously said the deal would include the reopening of the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route, without giving further details. The narrow waterway, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually passes, has been effectively closed since the conflict started on 28 February.
Trump said on Saturday that an agreement would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, without giving further details.

"Final aspects and details of the deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly." He also said he had a call on Saturday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, which "went very well". The president did not give any further details on the deal, but has insisted any agreement would "absolutely" prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. But on Sunday, he said on Truth Social: "Both sides must take their time and get it right. There can be no mistakes!" Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei earlier told state television that US and Iranian positions had been converging in the last week, but warned that did not mean agreements would be reached on key issues and accused the Americans of "contradictory statements".

The Nikkei 225 stock index in Japan rose above 65,000 for the first time after gaining 3% on hopes that the strait would soon reopen. Japan, like nearby South Korea, has been particularly impacted by the conflict as they are heavily reliant on energy from the Gulf. UK and US energy and financial markets are closed on Monday for public holidays. Trump said on social media on Saturday that he had a "very good call" with the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and others about a "Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE". "An agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed," Trump said.

payload.title: Öljyn hinta laski jyrkästi Hormuzinsalmen avaamiseen liittyvien toiveiden vuoksi
payload.summary: Öljyn maailmanmarkkinahinta laski Aasiassa, kun markkinoilla arvioitiin Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välisen sopimuksen voivan avata uudelleen Hormuzinsalmen ja lieventää alueen konfliktin vaikutuksia energiakuljetuksiin.
payload.content:
Öljyn hinta on laskenut selvästi ja Aasian osakemarkkinat ovat nousseet, kun sijoittajat ovat reagoineet toiveisiin sopimuksesta, joka voisi päättää Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin sodan Irania vastaan sekä avata uudelleen Hormuzinsalmen. Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump sanoi lauantaina, että sopimus Teheranin kanssa oli pitkälti neuvoteltu, mutta kehotti seuraavana päivänä neuvottelijoita olemaan kiirehtimättä ratkaisua.

## Öljy halpeni Aasian kaupankäynnissä

Maanantaina Aasiassa kansainvälinen Brent-viiteöljy oli 5,5 prosentin laskussa 97,90 dollarissa barrelilta. Yhdysvalloissa kaupattava raakaöljy oli puolestaan 5,9 prosenttia alempana 90,93 dollarissa.

Hintojen laskun taustalla on odotus siitä, että Hormuzinsalmi voitaisiin avata uudelleen osana mahdollista sopimusta. Trump on sanonut aiemmin, että sopimus sisältäisi salmen avaamisen, mutta hän ei ole kertonut tarkempia ehtoja. Kapea meriväylä on ollut käytännössä suljettuna konfliktin alettua 28. helmikuuta.

Hormuzinsalmella on suuri merkitys maailman energiamarkkinoille, sillä sen kautta kulkee tavallisesti noin viidennes maailman öljystä ja nesteytetystä maakaasusta. Sulun vaikutukset ovat tuntuneet erityisesti maissa, jotka ovat riippuvaisia Persianlahden energiatoimituksista.

## Neuvottelujen aikataulu on yhä epäselvä

Trump sanoi lauantaina, että sopimuksen viimeisiä yksityiskohtia käsitellään ja että niistä kerrotaan pian. Hän kertoi myös puhuneensa Israelin pääministerin Benjamin Netanyahun kanssa ja kuvasi puhelua myönteisesti. Trumpin mukaan mahdollisen sopimuksen olisi myös estettävä Irania saamasta ydinasetta.

Sunnuntaina Trump kuitenkin viestitti, ettei ratkaisua pidä kiirehtiä. Hän kirjoitti sosiaalisessa mediassa, että molempien osapuolten on otettava aikaa ja vältettävä virheitä.

Iranin ulkoministeriön edustaja Esmaeil Baqaei sanoi aiemmin valtiollisessa televisiossa, että Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin kannat ovat lähentyneet viime viikon aikana. Samalla hän varoitti, ettei se vielä tarkoita sopua keskeisistä kysymyksistä, ja syytti Yhdysvaltoja ristiriitaisista lausunnoista.

Japanissa Nikkei 225 -osakeindeksi nousi yli 65 000 pisteen ensimmäistä kertaa, kun se vahvistui kolme prosenttia salmen avaamiseen liittyvien odotusten tukemana. Japani ja Etelä-Korea ovat kärsineet tilanteesta erityisesti, koska ne ovat vahvasti riippuvaisia Persianlahden energiasta. Britannian ja Yhdysvaltojen energia- ja rahoitusmarkkinat ovat maanantaina kiinni yleisten vapaapäivien vuoksi.
summary_bullets: Brent-öljy laski Aasiassa 5,5 prosenttia ja Yhdysvalloissa kaupattava raakaöljy 5,9 prosenttia.
Markkinat reagoivat toiveisiin sopimuksesta, joka voisi avata Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen.
Trump on sanonut sopimuksen olevan pitkälti neuvoteltu, mutta kehotti myöhemmin olemaan kiirehtimättä ratkaisua.

Oil prices have fallen sharply and Asian stock markets have risen on hopes of a deal that could bring an end to the US-Israel war with Iran. On Saturday, US President Donald Trump said an agreement with Tehran had been "largely negotiated" and details would be announced soon but the following day urged his negotiating team not to rush a deal. On Monday in Asia, global oil benchmark Brent was down by 5.5% at $97.90 (£72.64), while US-traded crude was 5.9% lower at $90.93. Trump had previously said the deal would include the reopening of the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route, without giving further details. The narrow waterway, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually passes, has been effectively closed since the conflict started on 28 February.

Trump said on Saturday that an agreement would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, without giving further details.

"Final aspects and details of the deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly." He also said he had a call on Saturday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, which "went very well". The president did not give any further details on the deal, but has insisted any agreement would "absolutely" prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. But on Sunday, he said on Truth Social: "Both sides must take their time and get it right. There can be no mistakes!" Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei earlier told state television that US and Iranian positions had been converging in the last week, but warned that did not mean agreements would be reached on key issues and accused the Americans of "contradictory statements".

The Nikkei 225 stock index in Japan rose above 65,000 for the first time after gaining 3% on hopes that the strait would soon reopen. Japan, like nearby South Korea, has been particularly impacted by the conflict as they are heavily reliant on energy from the Gulf. UK and US energy and financial markets are closed on Monday for public holidays. Trump said on social media on Saturday that he had a "very good call" with the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and others about a "Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE". "An agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed," Trump said.
